headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra can write and egress broadly while Marker is local-only, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, injection, and downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write files, read files, and pass data through stdin/stdout and workflows; Marker can process documents but has no shared channel documented. The pair lacks a proven default bridge, yet a shared filesystem or manual handoff could let attacker-controlled document content influence downstream parsing. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF Kestra writes Marker-consumed documents into a shared directory
IF Marker ingests Kestra-produced files as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use separate directories for Kestra outputs and Marker inputs
Add a manual review step before Marker processes Kestra-generated files
Prefix all machine-generated files with a non-executable marker header
Restrict Kestra to writing only to a staging folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Marker is local-only with no network egress, so the main leakage path is Kestra exporting sensitive data into documents or outputs that Marker then processes. This is plausible in default orchestration setups, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Kestra routes sensitive workflow data into files that Marker reads
IF Marker outputs derived text back into a shared report or notification channel
mitigations: Limit Kestra inputs to non-sensitive samples
Store Marker inputs in a separate access-controlled folder
Disable exporting sensitive fields in Kestra logs and artifacts
Review any shared notification destinations before running the pair
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has broad write and execution capabilities, while Marker has no filesystem write, shell, or network egress. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict risk is limited unless an operator gives both access to the same mutable workspace. The pair is not fully isolated, but the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF Kestra is configured to mutate files that Marker also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run Marker read-only
Avoid shared git worktrees
Serialize any file updates through one agent at a time
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that Marker may later consume as documents. Marker does not show built-in verification of upstream facts, so a bad Kestra output can cascade into incorrect document processing or reporting. The pathway is plausible but not proven to trigger autonomous actions.
conditions: IF Marker treats Kestra-produced text as authoritative input
IF Kestra emits malformed or misleading workflow artifacts
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Kestra and Marker
Require human review of Kestra outputs before Marker ingestion
Use schema checks on exchanged files
Keep generated summaries separate from source documents
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance metadata to handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source, but Kestra touches database, cloud storage, messages, and notifications while Marker's profile shows no touched data classes or residency controls. The main compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch if regulated data is routed through Kestra and then processed by Marker without documented retention or residency handling. The other agent is not cited because no specific compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra into Marker without a retention policy
IF Marker outputs are stored in a jurisdictionally restricted system
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention for Kestra artifacts and Marker outputs
Keep jurisdiction-sensitive data out of shared folders
Review vendor terms before production use
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
